emma: Quick Q — my spouse just got laid off and lost their employer health plan effective today. Can I add them mid-year as a QLE? I saw 30 days but how strict is that?
maya_peopleops: Sorry to hear that, Emma. Yes, involuntary loss of employer coverage qualifies as a QLE. You have 30 days from the loss date to submit enrollment.
emma: Ok great. What proof do you need?
maya_peopleops: We need a termination letter/email or employer COBRA notice showing coverage ended, OR an insurer denial showing termination date. Upload via Workday -> Benefits -> Upload eligibility docs. PDF preferred.
emma: If I enroll them, when does coverage start? Is it retro to the loss date?
sam_peopleops: Typically coverage is effective the date after the other plan ends or the date you request (depending on the plan rules). For most cases we make it effective the day after the employer plan termination, so there is no coverage gap. We'll confirm once we verify docs.
emma: Will payroll deduct premiums retroactively? I have already hit my pre-tax max for the month.
payroll: Heads up: mid-month elections may create prorated premiums and possible retro deductions. If your spouse is not an IRS dependent, employer portion may be imputed income. We'll run a net-pay estimate and DM you the numbers before finalizing.
emma: Any impact on my FSA/HSA?
maya_peopleops: FSA mid-year election changes for QLEs are allowed for dependent care or health FSA? usually yes for eligibility changes. HSA contribution limits don't change but if you switch plan types (HSA-eligible to non-HSA), you may need to stop contributions. We'll flag your case for an FSA/HSA admin review.
benefits-bot: Automated: QLE case created #RB-QLE-2025-789. Expected review SLA: 2 business days. Please upload docs within 30 days to avoid denial.
emma: Uploaded the termination email and COBRA notice. Thanks for the quick replies.
maya_peopleops: Got it. We'll review and respond within 2 business days. If anything's missing we'll ping you.
emma: Thank you all :pray:
